### You Can’t Talk People Out of Their Pain
Author: Rick Warren
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/daily-hope-with-rick-warren/daily-hope-with-rick-warren-september-30-2020.html
Passage: Job 2:13
Points:
- Effective listening requires a patient, unhurried investment of time.
- In severe crisis and deep grief, the fewer words spoken, the better.
- People cannot be talked out of profound pain, making silent presence vital.
- True friends show up and wait patiently until the sufferer is ready to speak.

### When Words Don’t Work
Author: Chrystal Evans Hurst
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-april-21-2017.html
Passage: Job 2:13
Points:
- Overwhelming life crises frequently leave people speechless, making physical presence far more impactful than words.
- Job's companions initially ministered well by entering his sorrow and remaining silent for seven days without offering explanations.
- People often stay away from hurting friends because they mistakenly believe they must provide answers or solve the problem.
- Quietly sitting, listening, and sharing tears offers genuine comfort when verbal advice falls flat.
